gholam.text:
ببین رفیق، تیم سوچانک و رفقاش یه ابزار خفن به اسم Expand Fetch دادن بیرون که کارش اسکرپ و وب‌گردی برای ایجنت‌های هوش مصنوعیه و قراره کلاً بازی رو عوض کنه. قضیه اینه که ایجنت‌ها تا حالا وب رو درست‌حسابی نمی‌دیدن و تو جواب دادن به سوالای ساده هم گیج می‌زدن، واسه همین اینا دو تا مدل ردیف کردن؛ یکی «آیریس» که مثل چشم آدمیزاد صفحه، جدول‌ها و آیکون‌ها رو می‌بینه و دومی «اکس‌ری» که دیتای مخفی پشت صحنه رو به صورت جیسون می‌کشه بیرون. تو تست‌هاشون روی بیش از هزار تا سوال سخت وب، این ابزار تونسته رکورد ۷۴ درصد دقت رو بزنه، در حالی که رقیب قبلیش فقط ۵۵ درصد گرفته بود، قیمتش هم هزار تا فچ به ازای یک دلاره و قشنگ نشون میده ایجنت چی رو از کجا خونده.

اهمیتش اینه که دیگه هوش مصنوعی‌ها موقع وب‌گردی کورمال‌کورمال نمی‌رن و با دیدن ظاهر واقعی صفحات و دیتای پشتشون، سوتی‌هاشون تو تحلیل سایت‌ها به حداقل می‌رسه.

Introducing Expand Fetch, a new way to scrape and crawl the web.

Your agent has never seen the web. No wonder it gets basic questions wrong.

Traditional Markdown APIs lose critical details. So we trained two System one models to change that:

Iris, a vision model that sees pages like you do, preserving tables, icons, and layouts.

X-Ray, a JSON model that uncovers the hidden data behind every page.

Every fetch also comes with a Wayback Machine. Every line links back to its source, so you can verify exactly what your agent saw.

Three products. One API.

On our benchmark of 1,094 questions across 326 challenging web pages, agents using Expand got 74% right. The next best API got 55%.

Available today at $1 per 1,000 fetches.

Try it at http://expand.ai

links.text:
Let your agent 
see the web
Fetch and crawl with frontier system one models.
Frontier models can't answer 
basic questions about the web.
Benchmarked Performance
How we measured
MDBench Hardv1
A set of hard web extraction cases that we curated together with our customers. They span enrichment, procurement, pricing and competitive intelligence, among other areas.
It intentionally targets what existing web-to-Markdown systems get wrong.
It is a question-answering benchmark: an agent gets only the page Markdown that each API returns and answers a question about what it says.
Tested on October 8, 2026.
Try it on any page.
Paste a URL, or open one of the examples, and see what your agent gets back.
Instant web data on tap.
Fetch a page, crawl a site, or subscribe to changes.
Every page comes with accurate Markdown, plus the hidden JSON and a snapshot you can cite.
- Iris Jev for the web. Iris is a vision model for the web. It reads the rendered page like you do and writes the main content as accurate Markdown. Navigation and footers go to the , one call away. The rest is noise, so it goes. Iris docs
- X-Ray The hidden data, without a browser. Coordinates, flight gates and diagrams often live in JSON the page loads, not in its HTML. X-Ray, our second System 1 model, finds the parts that matter and drops the rest. X-Ray docs
- Wayback Machine Every fetch becomes an asset you own. Verify every answer precisely. Every line links back to the element on the page it came from, even after the site changes. Hover to debug. Share to cite. Wayback Machine docs
- Highlights Let your agent focus on what matters. If your agent already knows what it's looking for, Highlights saves over 95% of tokens with no loss in accuracy. Pass a query and get back only the passages that answer it. 
  - Faster TTFT
  - Zero noise
Highlights docs
- Crawl anything with one command. Our crawler scales to millions of pages, so you don't need to manage state or processes. No extra cost for crawling: each page is one credit, the same as a Fetch.
- A syncing engine for the web. WebSync rechecks every page on your schedule and streams each change as an event: a page added, a page changed with its diff, a page removed with the evidence. 
  - Monitor a site for changes
  - A constant change feed
  - A durable stream you can resume from where you left off
Give your agent a brain on disk: a Markdown file per page, kept in sync.
Let your agent pay attention to what matters.
Progressive disclosure
The best of both worlds.
Other tools make you choose the full page or a trimmed one. Your agent reads the main content first and asks for the rest only when it needs it: nothing lost, far fewer tokens.
Lossless
Nothing is thrown away.
Existing web-to-Markdown tools follow hard-coded rules and lose crucial details in the conversion. The web is too complex for rules.
If something is still missing, progressive disclosure has you covered.
Token efficient
24% fewer tokens at scale.
At 5 million requests a month on Gemini 4, that is $576K a year.*
*With JSON mode off. Input tokens only; the output is the same either way.
Other Markdown APIs
20,000 tokens a page · 100B tokens
Expand, JSON mode off
15,200 tokens a page · 76B tokens
($2/M input, $10/M output)You save ~$576,000 a year
Getting Started
It works out of the box without any configuration—JavaScript rendering, residential proxies, and bot protection are handled automatically for every request.
Pricing 
Only pay for what you need
Pay as you go
Popular
Prepaid credits, $1 per 1,000.
Pay only for what you need. No monthly commitments.
FAQ
Questions
Isn't turning a web page into Markdown a solved problem?
It works for a news article and breaks on many other layouts. Converters guess the main content with fixed rules, the way reader mode does. On a pricing table, a product page or a dashboard, that guess drops the icons, flattens the table and misses the data the page loads. Iris looks at the rendered page instead, every element with its position, size and weight, and sorts each one into preserve, prune or appendix.
Why not hand my agent the raw HTML, or a browser?
Raw HTML is mostly markup and scripts your agent pays tokens to read, and a JavaScript app arrives as an empty shell. A browser with screenshots works, but it is slow and expensive, and the tokens add up fast. Expand renders the page in a real browser for you and returns what it shows as Markdown, at API speed.
How do I know what my agent actually read?
Each browser page fetch saves the captured page with every asset. Open expand.land/s/<snapshotId>/playground and click any line of the Markdown to see where it came from on the page, even after the site has changed. Share the link to cite it.
What is the hidden JSON?
The data behind what a page shows, including values that never appear as text: a product's price, rating and stock, the coordinates on a map, a flight's gate. X-Ray reads that JSON, keeps the parts a question could be asked about and drops the
